internal.title: Investigation and Escalation of Frontend Service Error Rate Alert
internal.body: At 12:11 UTC, an alert was triggered indicating a high error rate in the frontend service. Initial diagnosis rounds analyzed hypotheses including error injection, latency issues, and resource exhaustion within the frontend service. Metrics consistently showed normal error ratios (0.01), latency below thresholds, and stable CPU and memory usage, contradicting the alert. Further investigation considered related services such as checkout but found no supporting evidence for errors originating there. Due to the lack of conclusive evidence supporting any hypothesis, the incident was escalated to the on-call engineer at 12:31 UTC for deeper investigation.

external.title: Frontend Service Alert Investigation Underway
external.body: We received an alert indicating a potential increase in errors in our frontend service. Our team promptly investigated the issue by reviewing service metrics and logs. Current data shows normal error rates and performance, and no impact to customer experience has been detected. We continue to monitor the situation closely and will provide updates if any issues are confirmed.

output.summary: An alert for high error rate in the frontend service was investigated but metrics showed normal operation, leading to escalation for further analysis.
output.impact: No confirmed impact to customers as frontend error rates and latency remained normal during the alert period.
output.root_cause: Root cause could not be determined based on available evidence; all tested hypotheses were contradicted by normal service metrics.
output.resolution: The incident was escalated to the on-call engineer for further investigation due to inconclusive findings from initial diagnosis.
